title: Minimum Number of Operations to Convert Time
summary: Given two 24-hour time strings, current and correct, determine the least number of operations required to convert current to correct by adding 1, 5, 15, or 60 minutes in any combination.
statement: Given two 24-hour time strings, current and correct, determine the least number of operations required to convert current to correct by adding 1, 5, 15, or 60 minutes in any combination.
constraints: Both times use 24-hour HH:MM format and current is not later than correct.
One operation adds exactly 1, 5, 15, or 60 minutes.
Return the fewest additions needed; the interval never wraps past midnight.
hints: Convert each clock string to minutes after midnight and take the nonnegative difference.
Always consume the largest allowed increment that fits the remaining difference.
For steps 60,15,5,1, use divmod and add each quotient to the operation count.
Each larger increment equals an integer number of smaller increments but costs only one operation, so replacing smaller groups proves descending greedy is optimal.
editorial: Each larger increment equals an integer number of smaller increments but costs only one operation, so replacing smaller groups proves descending greedy is optimal.

tests.explanation: Two sixty-minute additions and one five-minute addition use three operations.
A single one-minute addition reaches the target.
